title: Electrochemistry Cell with Voltage Control and Particle Effects
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D electrochemistry cell simulation using Three.js with voltage control and particle effects. The entire scene must be in a single HTML file.

SCENE SETUP:
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8), looking at origin
- Lighting: Ambient light (0x404040, intensity 0.5) + DirectionalLight (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at (5, 10, 5)
- Background: Dark gradient (0x1a1a2e)
- OrbitControls for camera rotation

ELECTROCHEMISTRY CELL:
- A transparent rectangular container (glass-like material, 4x3x2 units) centered at origin representing the electrolyte solution
- Left electrode (anode): Red metallic cylinder (radius 0.2, height 2.5) at x=-1.2, partially submerged
- Right electrode (cathode): Blue metallic cylinder (radius 0.2, height 2.5) at x=1.2, partially submerged
- A wire connecting the tops of both electrodes (curved line using TubeGeometry)
- Electrolyte solution: Semi-transparent blue-tinted volume inside the container

PARTICLE SYSTEM:
- Cations (positive ions): Small red spheres (radius 0.05) that move toward the cathode when voltage is applied
- Anions (negative ions): Small blue spheres (radius 0.05) that move toward the anode when voltage is applied
- Electrons: Tiny yellow spheres (radius 0.03) flowing through the wire from anode to cathode
- Particle count: 30 cations, 30 anions, 20 electrons in wire
- When voltage is 0, ions drift randomly (Brownian motion). When voltage > 0, ions migrate with velocity proportional to voltage
- Particle speed = voltage * 0.3 units/second for ions, voltage * 0.8 for electrons
- Bubbles: When voltage >= 2.0V, generate small white bubble particles at cathode (hydrogen evolution), rising upward

VOLTAGE CONTROL:
- A DOM slider input (range 0.0 to 5.0V, step 0.1) labeled 'Voltage (V)'
- A DOM display showing current voltage value
- Keyboard: Arrow Up increases voltage by 0.5V, Arrow Down decreases by 0.5V (clamped 0-5)
- Keyboard 'R' resets voltage to 0 and resets all particles to random positions
- Keyboard 'P' toggles pause/resume of the simulation
- Keyboard 'S' toggles between standard view and cross-section view (hides front face of container)

PHYSICS & CHEMISTRY:
- Current (I) = voltage * conductivity, where conductivity = 0.5 A/V
- Power dissipated = voltage * current (Joule heating)
- Electrolyte temperature starts at 25°C, increases by power * 0.1 per second (capped at 100°C)
- When temperature > 80°C, electrolyte color shifts toward orange/red tint
- Faraday's law: mass deposited at cathode = (current * time * molarMass) / (n * F), track cumulative charge passed
- Conservation: total particle count must remain constant (no particles created or destroyed, only repositioned)

HUD/UI:
- Top-left panel showing: Voltage, Current, Power, Temperature, Cumulative Charge (in Coulombs)
- A 'Reset' button that resets all state to initial
- A 'Reverse Polarity' button that swaps anode/cathode behavior (ions reverse direction)
- All values update in real-time

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
- voltage: current voltage (number, 0-5)
- current: calculated current in Amps
- power: power in Watts
- temperature: electrolyte temperature in Celsius
- cumulativeCharge: total charge passed in Coulombs
- particleCount: {cations: number, anions: number, electrons: number}
- isPaused: boolean
- isReversed: boolean (polarity reversed)
- isCrossSection: boolean
- bubbleActive: boolean (true when voltage >= 2.0)
- elapsedTime: simulation time in seconds
- avgCationX: average x-position of cations (should drift toward cathode)
- avgAnionX: average x-position of anions (should drift toward anode)
- totalParticles: total number of all particles (must be conserved at 80)
- electrodeDeposit: mass deposited at cathode in grams
- conductivity: 0.5 (constant)
- resetCount: number of times reset has been triggered
physics_constraints: Ohm's law: I = V * conductivity (0.5 A/V). Power = V * I. Temperature rise = power * 0.1 per second, capped at 100°C. Faraday's law for electrode deposition. Particle conservation: total particles always equals 80. Ion migration velocity proportional to applied voltage. Bubble generation threshold at 2.0V. All numerical values must be NaN-free.
